objectives.wording: Trace a specimen from clinical question through diagnosis and explain how pathology informs management.
Define common pathology terms and identify milestones in the discipline's development.
Map the phases and checkpoints of the cell cycle and explain how their control relates to growth and repair.
Explain how stem cells support tissue renewal and repair and outline principles of regenerative medicine.
Classify major insults and link mechanisms of injury to cellular and clinical consequences.
Describe the etiology of cell injury, then distinguish reversible from irreversible injury by mechanism and by the morphology of the injured cell.
Identify patterns of injury on gross and microscopic specimens and explain their likely consequences.
Distinguish lipid, protein, carbohydrate and pigment accumulation on representative images.
Compare the mechanisms and morphological patterns of necrosis and distinguish necrosis from autolysis.
Compare the mechanisms and morphology of apoptosis with necrosis.
Compare dystrophic and metastatic calcification by mechanism, setting and morphology.
Distinguish dry, wet and gas gangrene by mechanism and morphology.
Compare atrophy, hypertrophy, hyperplasia and metaplasia by stimulus, mechanism and morphology.
Distinguish dysplasia from carcinoma in situ and explain its significance as a precursor lesion.
